speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Regular singular D-modules and gluing
summary: The actual entry begins on P001060, after the preceding Liouville discussion. Gelfand recalls the Lorentz-group reduction to linear algebra; Beilinson then describes regular singular modules on a punctured disk and gluing across a closed subvariety. The final relation \(vu=N\) is shorthand, not a complete definition. Beilinson’s later paper explicitly says it follows S. I. Gelfand’s 1982 notes \citep[introduction]{beilinson1987glue}.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Continuous-dimensional Grassmannians and a Schubert analogy
summary: The intervention occupies the top of P001061. Gelfand recalls finite Grassmannian cells, then asks about fixed-trace projections in a type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor, continuous flags, monotone parameters, topology and cohomology. The notebook expressly calls the problem imprecise, so these questions are preserved as a programme rather than assigned a fabricated solved/open theorem.

speaker: Yu. I. Manin
title: Twistor geometry and flag superspaces
summary: The entry occupies P001061--P001063. After an agenda extending to supersymmetric field equations, Manin recalls the Grassmannian model of compactified complex Minkowski space, formulates a classification problem for flag superspaces, and explains the functor of points and two examples. The surviving text stops at the opening of the Penrose correspondence; it contains no worked new Yang--Mills solution. The closely related 1983 chapter is identifiable, but its full classification has not been verified here \citep{manin1983flags}.

speaker: A. M. Polyakov
title: Liouville uniformization, accessory parameters and Virasoro blocks
summary: The talk occupies P001064--P001069. It moves from the Liouville action and cusp uniformization to the stress tensor, accessory parameters, and the proposed recovery of classical geometry from quantum Ward identities. The last pages give a Verma-module expansion and an oscillator realization. The classical generating-function conjecture was proved by Zograf and Takhtajan; the conformal-block programme appears in BPZ 1984, while rigorous sphere Liouville construction and bootstrap came much later. Several factors, powers and completeness relations in the notebook are inconsistent and are explicitly corrected below.

speaker: I. Yu. Kobzarev
title: Domain walls, vortex strings and the Nambu action
summary: The actual talk is P001070--P001073. A scalar double well supplies a planar wall; the Abelian Higgs model supplies a vortex string. Integrating a thin core yields the Nambu worldsheet action, with a collapsing circular loop as an illustration. The final page introduces the colour gauge Lagrangian. These are expository constructions predating the talk; the wall formula can be checked against Kobzarev’s own 1974 paper. The notes suppress couplings and contain a gauge-sign mismatch.

title: Year 1983
summary: This MCCME record is a year heading. It has no separate mathematical content; the adjacent February material belongs to records 580 and 581.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Near-unitary circle actions and Fock-space representations
summary: The record occupies the upper part of P001074. Following Gelfand’s methodological and supersymmetry remarks, Kirillov reports Neretin’s weighted pullbacks, their Hilbert--Schmidt failure of unitarity, and Gaussian/Fock unitarization. This construction had already appeared in 1982; extending the action on the original one-particle space and constructing a new unitary action on Fock space must be distinguished \citep{neretin1982complementary}.

speaker: B. L. Feigin
title: String constraints and semi-infinite homology
summary: The actual notes occupy the lower P001074 and P001075. They pass from the loop-space symplectic form to oscillator quantization, explain the central-term obstruction to ordinary invariants, and replace invariants by the image of positive-mode invariants in negative-mode coinvariants. Feigin’s 1984 note identifies this physical-state construction with semi-infinite homology. Gelfand’s closing p-adic request has a separately documented answer in Neretin’s 1984 paper.

speaker: Yu. A. Neretin
title: Hilbert transforms, almost invariant kernels and circle representations
summary: The entry is P001076--P001077, including a name of Ginzburg crossed out before the final continuation question. The 1982 near-orthogonal construction is refined by endpoint complex structures and restricted symplectic actions, published in Neretin’s 1983 Doklady note. Gelfand’s pseudodifferential generalization remains unspecified. The written logarithmic convolution cannot yield the claimed derivative of a delta distribution; the Fock-space question needs a completed symmetric space rather than arbitrary analytic sequences.

speaker: V. L. Ginzburg
title: Duistermaat--Heckman localization and orbital integrals
summary: The entry occupies P001078 and the upper part of P001079. It presents Hamiltonian torus actions, regular reduction, affine variation of reduced symplectic classes, polynomial densities and exact stationary phase, then relates these to convexity and characters. The 1982 theorem is expository here. The nonisolated fixed-component formula is abbreviated beyond validity: normal-bundle curvature terms are needed. The historical allusions to Semenov-Tian-Shansky and Vergne have identifiable pre-talk sources.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: The SU(3) orbit hexagon and weight multiplicities
summary: The intervention begins in the lower part of P001079 and ends with a single request on P001080. It revisits the six-dimensional regular orbit, its torus-moment hexagon and changes in the fibers. The written map uses two conjugacy invariants and therefore cannot produce that hexagon; diagonal projection is the required interpretation. The final weight-multiplicity request recurs from 1981-556 and retains GP-1981-41.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Mathieu gaps, Catalan diagrams and spectral perturbation
summary: The actual talk is P001081--P001086; P001080 belongs to Kirillov and P001087 begins Krichever. Arnold explains delayed splitting of Hill eigenvalues for trigonometric-polynomial perturbations by quiver paths, Catalan bracket fillings and a reversal involution. The paper received on 1 February 1983 and published later that year closely matches the talk. Its 30 March supplement acknowledges older results of Bloch, Levy--Keller and Hochstadt, so the estimates and coefficient identities are not all classified as new 1983 discoveries. Gelfand’s one-gap question remains underdetermined in this record.
